findings.title: Dynamic imports still load every app at module init
findings.body: Every app is started with a top-level import() inside the appStore object literal, so evaluating this module immediately begins loading all app packages. Callers cannot load only the app they need, which defeats the stated async-import goal: startup still pays for every integration, and a failed chunk becomes a rejected promise on that key the first time it is awaited. Wrap each entry in a function (e.g. applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")) and invoke it only at the lookup site.

findings.title: async forEach drops calendar and video deletion
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not wait for the callback. getCalendar is now async, so the first await yields before deleteEvent or deleteMeeting is even called, and the returned promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot see rejections. Reschedule then sends the email and returns while cleanup is still pending, so on a short-lived server the old calendar event and video meeting are often never deleted and failures are unhandled. Await Promise.all over the refs (or use for...of) and await both getCalendar and deleteMeeting.

findings.title: async forEach drops calendar and video deletion
findings.body: Same pattern as vital reschedule: forEach(async) is not joined. Because getCalendar must be awaited, calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting are no longer even started before Reschedule returns and the try/catch cannot catch their errors. Previous-slot calendar events and video meetings are left behind on reschedule. Replace forEach with an awaited Promise.all or for...of.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for integration cleanup
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) fires getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting without awaiting the callbacks. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and completes. Those promises are not part of the procedure's returned work, so calendar deletes and video deletes are raced against process exit and their rejections are unhandled. The booking is already marked CANCELLED, so a dropped delete leaves a ghost event on the user's calendar. Await Promise.all of the per-reference work before sendRequestRescheduleEmail.

findings.title: Recurring cancel never joins calendar deletes
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining recurring instances, credentials are walked with forEach(async). getCalendar and deleteEvent are awaited only inside that callback, and apiDeletes.push runs after those awaits. The later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) therefore runs before any of those pushes, so recurring calendar events are not deleted and errors never fail the handler. The non-recurring branch correctly uses a for...of and pushes the promise before awaiting the batch; this branch should do the same (or return promises into apiDeletes without an inner await).
